title: Exercise and the Body
hook: Physical activity reaches far beyond muscle — it strengthens the heart, reshapes metabolism, and even sharpens the brain.
key_points: Exercise makes muscles stronger and improves their endurance.
It strengthens the heart, so it pumps more blood with each beat.
Activity helps control weight, blood sugar, and blood pressure.
It also boosts mood, memory, and brain health.
content_html: It's easy to think of exercise as just a way to build muscle, but its effects ripple through nearly every system in the body. Working muscles get stronger and more enduring, but the same activity also trains the heart, tunes metabolism, and even changes the brain.
extra_html: As MedlinePlus describes, the heart is itself a muscle, so aerobic activity strengthens it — letting it pump more blood with each beat and work less hard at rest. Regular movement helps control body weight, keeps blood sugar and blood pressure in healthier ranges, and strengthens bones. The benefits reach the brain too: exercise boosts blood flow and releases chemicals that lift mood, ease anxiety, and support memory and learning. Taken together, that's why staying active is one of the most reliable things a person can do to lower the risk of chronic disease and feel better day to day.

related.title: Bones and Muscles
related.hook: Your skeleton is the frame and your muscles are the engines — together they let you stand, move, and protect the soft organs inside you.

related.title: The Circulatory System
related.hook: Your heart pumps blood through roughly 60,000 miles of vessels, delivering oxygen and fuel to every cell and hauling waste away — about once a minute.

related.title: Diet and Disease
related.hook: What you eat over years quietly shapes your odds of heart disease, type 2 diabetes, and more — diet is one of the strongest levers on long-term health.

flashcards.prompt: Name three things regular exercise does for the body.
flashcards.back_html: It strengthens muscles, makes the heart pump more efficiently, and improves brain health and mood — plus it helps control weight, blood sugar, and blood pressure.

flashcards.prompt: What happens to the heart with regular aerobic exercise?

choices.text: It grows stronger and pumps more blood per beat
It shrinks until it can no longer pump

flashcards.explanation_html: The heart is a muscle. Regular activity strengthens it, so it moves more blood with each beat and doesn't have to work as hard at rest.

flashcards.prompt: How does exercise affect the brain?

choices.text: It can improve mood, memory, and thinking
It has no effect on the brain at all
It only affects the brain in children

flashcards.explanation_html: Exercise increases blood flow to the brain and triggers chemicals that lift mood and support memory and learning — benefits seen across all ages.
